image.label: Render
image.doc: The render, as computed. Pick which one in the bar above.

brightness.label: Brightness
brightness.doc: How bright each point is, as a grey field: a mix of luminance and the brightest channel (so a pure colour counts as bright), stretched and curved.

flow.label: Flow
flow.doc: The direction the picture's contours run (structure tensor): strokes, smears and trails follow it. Output is a direction field.

edges.label: Fringe density
edges.doc: How fast the picture changes here: dense fine fringes read bright. A stand-in for sensitivity until the data exists.

paper.label: Paper
paper.doc: A sheet of paper: colour, tooth and a few fibres.

smear.label: Smear along flow
smear.doc: Drag the image along the flow, both ways, fading with distance (line-integral convolution).

strokes.label: Strokes
strokes.doc: A field of tapered strokes laid along the flow: sparse dabs, dragged each way. Wire a grey field into density to put more strokes where it is bright.

kuwahara.label: Kuwahara
kuwahara.doc: Flatten colour into painterly passages: each point takes the calmest of the four squares around it.

relief.label: Relief light
relief.doc: Treat a grey field as the thickness of the paint and light it low from one side: shading, highlights, cast shadows and occlusion in the dips. Bright = thick.

levels.label: Colour
levels.doc: Exposure, contrast, saturation, warmth and lifted blacks.

neon.label: Neon
neon.doc: Light, not pigment: each colour pushed to full brightness, same hue, more saturated.

palette.label: Palette
palette.doc: Snap every colour to a limited palette (nearest in OKLab, hue counted more than lightness).

duotone.label: Duotone
duotone.doc: Two inks: lightness laid between a dark and a light colour.

mix.label: Mix
mix.doc: Combine two images: normal, multiply, screen, add or overlay; optionally only where a mask is bright.

glow.label: Film glow
glow.doc: What film does to bright light: bloom round its source, a red-orange halation halo, then exposure. Turn exposure and bloom up for a blown-out long exposure; threshold sets how bright light has to be before it blooms.

grain.label: Grain
grain.doc: Film grain, strongest in the mid-tones.

offset.label: Offset press
offset.doc: Four plates — cyan, magenta, yellow and a rich black — each slipping out of register, ink feathering into the stock (the 1978 NASA Facts poster).

halftone.label: Halftone
halftone.doc: AM halftone: each plate a screen of dots at its own angle (C 15°, M 75°, Y 0°, K 45°), dot size carrying the tone, rosettes where they meet.

riso.label: Risograph
riso.doc: Four drums — fluoro pink, blue, yellow, black — each a grainy screen, slightly out of register, inks multiplying.

dither.label: Dither
dither.doc: Ordered or random dithering on a coarse pixel grid: Bayer 2×2, 4×4, 8×8, random, or interleaved gradient noise; two or three colours, or each channel in its own colours.

dotmatrix.label: Dot matrix
dotmatrix.doc: An impact printer: bands of dots per pass, tone by ordered dither, the ribbon wearing down each band. Colour prints a four-colour ribbon (cyan, magenta, yellow, black) one band at a time, slightly out of register. Bands sets how strongly the passes show.

crt.label: CRT
crt.doc: An old CRT television: scanlines whose width follows brightness, an aperture grille of RGB phosphor stripes, misconvergence, glow, snow.

lcd.label: Old LCD
lcd.doc: A coarse LCD panel: RGB sub-pixels with the screen door between them, few colour bits dithered, backlight bleed at the edges.

gameboy.label: Game Boy
gameboy.doc: The original Game Boy screen: a few rows of pixels in four greens, dithered, a faint grid, each pixel's shadow on the backing.

mcmap.label: Block-game map
mcmap.doc: As if drawn on a block-game map: a coarse grid of map pixels, each snapped to the map palette (61 base colours, each in up to three shades), optionally with ordered dither.

mcblocks.label: Blocks
mcblocks.doc: Each cell replaced by the block-game block whose average colour is nearest: concrete, wool, terracotta, planks, ores, stone. The 16×16 textures are drawn procedurally, and tile the same way for every block of a kind.

ascii.label: ASCII
ascii.doc: The picture set in characters: each cell's brightness picks a glyph, from a ten-step character ramp ( .:-=+*#%@) in a 5×7 bitmap font, or from shade blocks. Mono terminal colours, the picture's own colours (optionally behind the glyphs too, like ANSI art), or ink on paper; own colours can be cut to a lower colour depth.

stipple.label: Stipple
stipple.doc: After Luminet's 1979 black hole: brightness drawn by hand as dots of ink, denser where brighter, printed as a negative (or as a positive).

pigment.label: Pigment wheel
pigment.doc: Electric screen colours pulled towards real watercolour pigments of the same hue; dark stays dark, greys stay grey.

invert.label: Invert lightness
invert.doc: A night print: lightness turned over, hue kept.

posterize.label: Flat colour
posterize.doc: Cut colour into flat passages with a few levels per channel, a slightly ragged cut edge and a darker rim where each passage dried (gouache).

watercolour.label: Watercolour wash
watercolour.doc: Transparent washes on paper: colour absorbed into the sheet, pigment pooling darker where one wash meets another, granulation, a soft bleed.

pencil.label: Pencil lines
pencil.doc: Lu, Xu & Jia's pencil: each edge drawn as a short line along its own direction, plus tonal hatching in the darks. Outputs a grey layer to multiply over a wash.

hatching.label: Graphite hatching
hatching.doc: Hatching that follows the forms, crossed in the darks, broken by the paper's tooth, burnished to a silver sheen where it is heaviest, a firmer contour where tone turns. Wide, dense strokes in black make it charcoal.

pastel.label: Chalk pastel
pastel.doc: Soft pastel on dark laid paper: colour laid with the side of the stick along the forms, catching only on the tooth unless pressed hard.

inkwash.label: Ink wash
inkwash.doc: Sumi-e: one ink at four dilutions, bleeding into the paper's fibres, pooling at each wash's edge, dry-brush breaks in the darkest strokes.

tempera.label: Egg tempera
tempera.doc: Thousands of tiny hatched strokes over white gesso, pale layers first and each closer to the true colour, then a glaze and fine craquelure.

engrave.label: Engraving
engrave.doc: Banknote line engraving: parallel lines that bend with the forms and swell where it is dark, crossed in the shadows, dots in the deepest blacks and a wiped plate tone.

mezzotint.label: Mezzotint
mezzotint.doc: A plate rocked all over so it prints a velvet black, with the lights scraped and burnished out; the grain is the rocker's short dashes in many directions.

linocut.label: Linocut
linocut.doc: A relief print: white gouges that follow the forms, more and wider where it is light, solid inked lands in the dark, a hand-burnished mottle.

cyanotype.label: Cyanotype
cyanotype.doc: Prussian blue and paper white, the sensitiser brushed on by hand so the coating streaks.

plotter.label: Pen plotter
plotter.doc: Fineliner lines that follow the forms, closer where darker, crossed in the shadows; each line in the pen nearest the colour under it.

marbling.label: Marbling
marbling.doc: Inks floated on size and combed through, then laid on paper: clean bands of colour with a pale dispersant ring at each edge, and a scatter of stones.

mosaic.label: Mosaic
mosaic.doc: Smalti set in grout: each tile one colour, slightly tilted, bevelled and glossy.

glass.label: Stained glass
glass.doc: Panes of streaky cathedral glass, cut along the picture's colour boundaries and a grid of cuts, leaded together and lit from behind.

kintsugi.label: Kintsugi
kintsugi.doc: The render as glazed ceramic, broken along its boundaries and mended with gold; crazing in the glaze and a window's reflection in its gloss.

cutpaper.label: Cut paper
cutpaper.doc: One sheet per tone, stacked by lightness, blade-cut, each sheet's lit edge catching the light and its shadow falling on the sheets beneath.

thread.label: Thread painting
thread.doc: Satin stitches along the forms on linen, each a raised twist of floss whose sheen changes with its direction.

polaroid.label: Polaroid
polaroid.doc: Instant film colour: lifted blacks, cyan-green shadows, warm highlights, softness, a light leak, grain. Full bleed.

thinfilm.label: Thin film
thinfilm.doc: The colours of oil on water: the picture sets the film's thickness, and each wavelength reflects from its two faces in or out of step.

negative.label: Film negative
negative.doc: A colour negative on the orange C-41 base, with grain, dust and fine scratches along the strip.

film35.label: 35mm film
film35.doc: Developed 35mm colour film, printed: an S-curve with soft lifted blacks, warm highlights and cool shadows, mid-tone grain, a vignette.

cracks.label: Craquelure
cracks.doc: An old painting's crack network, fine where the mask is strongest and coarser where it is moderate, with cupped edges catching the light. Wire fringe density (or real sensitivity data) into mask.

stereogram.label: Stereogram
stereogram.doc: A single-image random-dot stereogram (a Magic Eye picture): brightness becomes depth, brighter nearer. Each pixel is linked to the pixel one eye-separation to its left, less a little where the picture is near, and takes the colour at the end of its chain in the first strip; so every link holds exactly and the picture appears in depth when you look through the page (wall-eyed). The pattern is random dots, dots drawn in the picture's own colours, or the picture itself tiled as wallpaper. Smooth the depth to keep the fused surface clean.

teletext.label: Teletext
teletext.doc: A teletext page: a grid of character cells (40 by 25 by default), each a block-graphics character of 2×3 sextants, lit in one of the seven teletext colours on black, with one foreground colour per cell, chosen to fit the cell best. Contiguous or separated graphics; optional ordered dither between sextants.

crossstitch.label: Cross-stitch
crossstitch.doc: Counted cross-stitch on cream aida: each cell one X of stranded cotton, the lower leg laid first and the upper leg crossing it, each leg a twisted, rounded strand going down into the holes of the weave. Colours are matched to a 32-colour box of threads, or to the picture's own colours cut to a few levels; dark cells can be left as bare cloth.

bricks.label: Brick mosaic
bricks.doc: A mosaic of 1×1 toy-brick plates, seen from above: each plate snapped to the nearest of 24 stock brick colours, with its round stud lit from the top left, a highlight on the stud's rim and its shadow falling to the bottom right.

eink.label: E-ink
eink.doc: An e-reader's electrophoretic screen: sixteen greys from ink to a paper-grey white, reached by ordered dither, a faint inverted ghost of the page before (the panel never quite clears), and the slight grain of the microcapsules.

ledmatrix.label: LED matrix
ledmatrix.doc: A board of round LEDs on black, one per cell of the picture: full colour, or a single colour (amber, red, green) driven by brightness. Unlit LEDs show as dark lenses, lit ones burn white-hot at the centre and bloom into their neighbours.

knit.label: Knit (Fair Isle)
knit.doc: Stocking-stitch knitting, as in a Fair Isle jumper: each stitch a V of two rounded, plied legs of wool, one yarn per stitch, the colours drawn from a handful of Shetland shades, two colours by tone, or the picture's own colours cut to a few levels.

scope.label: Oscilloscope
scope.doc: The picture traced by a vector display's beam: contour lines of brightness at even steps, drawn in green phosphor on a dark tube, dimmer where the beam has to move fast across steep slopes, with the phosphor's glow around each trace.

crosshatch.label: Cross-hatching
crosshatch.doc: Pen and ink tone built from hatching: one set of parallel lines in the half-tones, crossed by a second, then a third and fourth on the diagonals as it darkens. The lines can be ruled straight or swept round the forms, each with a little wobble of the hand. Detail lifts local contrast so the forms still read where the picture is all mid-tones.

graphitepencil.label: Pencil
graphitepencil.doc: A graphite pencil on cartridge paper: soft grey strokes laid along the forms, the lead catching only the tops of the paper's tooth in the lights, rubbed and smudged into an even grey in the darks, with the silvery sheen of burnished graphite where it is heaviest. Grade runs from a hard, pale 2H to a soft, black 6B; detail lifts local contrast so the forms still read in the mid-tones.

fineliner.label: Fineliner
fineliner.doc: A technical pen: one even line weight, no pressure in it at all. The forms are drawn as contour lines of equal brightness, like a map's, and the tone is put in with stippled dots or short hatched dashes.

marker.label: Marker
marker.doc: Alcohol markers: broad, see-through strokes laid side by side along the forms, each in whichever pen of the set is nearest the colour beneath it. The ink pools darker at a stroke's edges and ends, streaks along the nib, and bleeds a little into the paper; where strokes overlap the colours multiply, and a second, crossing layer goes over the darker passages.

biro.label: Ballpoint
biro.doc: A blue biro: fine scribbled hatching, layer over layer at shifting angles, until the darks build to a dense blue-black with the oily shine of ballpoint ink. The ball skips here and there and leaves the odd blob. On plain, feint-ruled or squared paper; detail lifts local contrast so the forms still read in the mid-tones.

tetris.label: Tetris
tetris.doc: The picture rebuilt from falling blocks: a repeating patch of 25 interlocking tetrominoes (I, O, T, S, Z, J and L) tiles the whole frame, each piece coloured by whichever of the seven classic piece colours is nearest the picture under it, or by the picture's own colour, and each block bevelled with a light top edge and a shaded lower one.

shatter.label: Shattered glass
shatter.doc: The picture seen through broken glass: radial cracks running out from an impact with irregular rings between them, or a pane fallen into shards. Each shard sits at its own slight angle, so the picture behind it slips and splits into colour at the edges; the cracks catch the light; the glass is crushed white at the point of impact.

palslot.label: Palette
palslot.doc: The palette slot: colours mapped nearest, by lightness or by class.

ground.label: Ground
ground.doc: The surface: colour, with the tooth's height in alpha.

onground.label: On the ground
onground.doc: Lays the medium onto the chosen surface: absorbency, tooth, and how each surface takes ink, paint or light.

unfinished.label: Unfinished
unfinished.doc: How far into the picture the artist got: past that, only the pencil underdrawing.

age.label: Age
age.doc: What happened to it after: fading, yellowing, foxing, a fold, tape, stains, varnish, scratches, burn-in.

view.label: Viewing
view.doc: How the light falls on it. Every mode keeps the picture full-frame: no borders, no perspective, nothing added around it.
